trickyParts: The retag remedy had to be written twice. 'Run the retag again, a per-name read rather than a listing' is true on Secrets Manager, where DescribeSecret answers a write at once, but Secret Manager documents GetSecret as eventually consistent like its listing, so the first wording would have promised freshness the store does not give. What makes exit 0 meaningful there is not the read's consistency but the retag's own check that the kind it reads back is the kind it wrote — and that a retag may therefore need running more than once, which the page now says.

The ERROR line is operator-visible text, so changing it is a deployment-visible change even though no behaviour moved: the alarm table had to change with it, and anything pinning the old string had to be found before the push rather than by CI.
discoveredComplexity: Six comment-against-code defects in one change, across three sweeps, and the last four were found by the reviewer after I had written the rule down and applied it myself. The cause is the same every time: the sentence was true when written and the round that changed what it describes left it standing. The retro learning records it as a reviewer's check — read every comment in a diff against the code above it — rather than as a thing to remember, and my own miss is the evidence that remembering does not work.

A gate that contradicts the list it gates is worse than no gate, because it converts a careful reader's diligence into a wrong answer. The previous text listed three signals and then gated on a property only one of them has; a reader who skipped the list and waited unconditionally would have been safer than one who followed the instruction.
